questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. **

The police used tear gas to ______ the crowd.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'disperse'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence means that the police used tear gas **to move apart the crowd.**
 
• **Tear gas** is commonly used by law enforcement **to control riots and crowds**.(दंगों और भीड़ को नियंत्रित करने के लिए आमतौर पर कानून प्रवर्तन द्वारा आंसू गैस का उपयोग किया जाता है।)
 
• **Let's look at the meanings of the given words:**
 
 
• **Attack- **to use violence to try to hurt or kill somebody.(किसी को चोट पहुँचाने या मारने की कोशिश करने के लिए हिंसा का इस्तेमाल करना।)
 
• **Disburse-** to pay money to somebody from a large amount that has been collected for a purpose.(किसी उद्देश्य के लिए एकत्र की गई बड़ी राशि से किसी को धन देना।)
 
• **Collect- **to bring things together from different people or places.(विभिन्न लोगों या स्थानों से चीजों को एक साथ लाने के लिए।)
 
• **Disperse-** To make somebody move apart or go in different directions.(किसी को अलग करना या अलग-अलग दिशाओं में जाना।)
 
 
 
• From the meanings given, **'disperse' **is the grammatically and conceptually correct word for the blank.

 

**So, the complete sentence is-** *The police used tear gas to **disperse **the crowd.(*भीड़ को तितर-बितर करने के लिए पुलिस ने आंसू गैस के गोले छोड़े।)

questions.solution:

• Take something with a pinch of salt means **"to not completely believe something that you are told because you think it is unlikely to be true".**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'begin to'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us refer to this line from the passage, "But the mere thought of _____(3)______ on occasions like these would throw her _____(4)______ such a nervous state that a tiny muscle in the corner of her left eye would _____(5)_____ twitch."
 
• The word before the blank No 5 is **'would'** which is a **modal**.
 
• Modals are followed by **V1.**
 
• Only option 3 has v1 i.e **begin.**
 
• So, **'begin to'** is the correct option for blank No 5.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of modals:**

 
 
• Modals are auxiliary verbs which are used to express **certainty, possibility, willingness, obligation, ability, etc.**
 
• Modals never change their form i.e. we can't use **'s/es/ing/ed'** with them.
 
• Modals are followed by **bare infinitive** i.e v1 without to.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

For the last two years Shweta __has being__ diligently working with Rohingya refugees to create colourful table mats using their local weaving techniques.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'has been'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The usage of **'being'** is wrong in the given sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the** present perfect continuous tense** and **'has been'** is used in the present perfect continuous tense.
 
 
• **E.g.** Girish **has been** working in this company for two years.
 
 
 
• According to the rule and example that are given above, **'has been' **will be used in the **underlined part** of the sentence.

 ​

**Correct Sentence__:** *For the last two years Shweta **has been** diligently working with Rohingya refugees to create colourful table mats using their local weaving techniques.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **The present perfect continuous tense** shows that something started in the past and is continuing at the present time.
 
• The present perfect continuous is formed using the construction **"has/have been + v1 + ing + for/ since + time".**
 
 
• **E.g.** we **have been living** in this house **since **2007.
 
 
 
• **Usage of 'since' and 'for':**
 
 
• **Since** is used for a point of time. 
 
 
• Since Monday, since, 2002, since, last year.
 
 
 
• **For** is used for a period of time.
 
 
• For the last two years, for the last 3 weeks

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. Finally, she takes the decision to go searching for livelihood in the nearby town.

B. They are: Lakua and his wife, Nathuni.

C. The latter, burdened with a paralytic husband and two children, battles to survive.

D. The film ‘Wayfarers’ narrates the journey of a poor couple in Jharkhand.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'DBCA'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sentence **D **is** independent** of any other sentence as it is giving some general information about the film 'Wayfarers'. Hence, 'D' is the **first** sentence. 
 
• **'Lakua and his wife'** mentioned in sentence B refer to the phrase **'a poor couple' **in sentence D. Hence, 'B' follows 'D'.
 
• The phrase **'the latter burdened with a paralytic husband' **mentioned in the sentence C refers to **'Nathuni'** in sentence B. Hence, 'C' follows 'B'. 
 
• The adverb **'finally'** indicates that 'A' is the last sentence.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:**

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try **to comprehend the idea or theme** of the paragraph and **eliminate the irrelevant options**.
 
• Try to identify the opening **(independent sentence) **and closing sentences of the paragraph **(concluding sentence).**
 
• Try to identify the** mandatory pairs**. Two sentences can be connected through various **connectors and other determinants.** Identify the **pronouns** connecting the sentences with each other.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. **

You must make a choice immediately because there is few time left.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'few time left'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The usage of **'few' **is wrong with the word **'time'.**
 
• **'Time'** is an **uncountable noun.** 
 
• **'Few'** is a quantifier which means **'some; not many'** and is used with **countable nouns**.
 
 
• **E.g.** **Few** people understand this problem.
 
 
 
• **'Little' **is a quantifier which means **'some' **and is used with **uncountable nouns**.
 
 
• **E.g**. They had **little **money to spend.
 
 
 
• According to the rule and the examples given above,** 'little'** will be used instead of **'few' **in the given sentence.

 ​

**Correct Sentence__:** *You must make a choice immediately because there is **little **time left.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Uncountable nouns **are the nouns which cannot be counted. 

 
 
• **E.g.** Equipment, time, hair, furniture, scenery, information, work, etc.
 
 
 
• Uncountable nouns **cannot** be made **plural** by adding an 's' at the end.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. **

Chhattisgarh organised the first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ in January 2020.

options.text: The first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ was organised by Chhattisgarh in January 2020.
The first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ was being organised by Chhattisgarh in January 2020.
The first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ had been organised by Chhattisgarh in January 2020.
The first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ will be organised by Chhattisgarh in January 2020.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ was organised by Chhattisgarh in January 2020.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 We need to follow these instructions while changing the voice of an **'Assertive sentence'.**

 
 
• 
 Find the **subject and object** of the sentence and **exchange their places**; make changes in their **cases** as well if subject and object are **pronouns**.
 
 
• 
 Use preposition **by **before agent. (Chhattisgarh)
 
 
• 
 Use helping verb in passive form according to the tense of active form. **(Past indefinite - was/ were)**
 
 
• 
 Always use the **third form** of the main verb in passive form.
 
 
• 
 At last line up the remaining part.

 
 
 
 

**Following these steps, we finally get- ***The first-ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ was organised by the Chhattisgarh State in January 2020*.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the wrong **omission** of the article **'a' **in the given sentence.
 
• The indefinite article **'a/an' **is used when we refer to a single entity out of many of similar kind or to refer to a thing** in general**.
 
 
• **E.g.** I need **a** laptop.
 
• In the above-mentioned sentence, we are referring to a laptop **in general**. It can be any laptop out of many laptops.
 
 
 
• There may be many types of village cultures in Madhya Pradesh and the sentence given in the question is referring to one out of many types which is** not a specific type**.
 
• According to the rule and example that are given above, the article** 'a'** will be used **before** the word** 'type' **in the given sentence.

 

**Correct Sentence__:** *Subhash Gidwani is selling dolls, which are **a type** of Madhya Pradesh’s village culture, at the Annual Dastakar Bazaar, held in January every year in Delhi.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• **'Which'** is a relative pronoun.
 
• **A relative pronoun** is a word that introduces a dependent (or relative) clause and connects it to an independent clause.
 
 
• **E.g.** His best movie, **which** won several awards, was about the life of Gandhi.

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of given sentence.**

The foreigner said to the farmer, “Can you tell me the way to the nearest hotel?”

options.text: The foreigner exclaimed with the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner suggested the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner asked the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner told the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The foreigner asked the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While changing the narration of an **interrogative sentence**, we need to follow the given steps-

 
 
• The conjunction **‘if’ **should be used in place of a comma (,) and inverted commas (“ ”).
 
• **'Question mark (?)'** is changed to full stop **(.).**
 
• **‘Said to’ **will be changed into **‘asked’**.
 
• **'Can' **is changed to **'could'.**
 
• **2nd person **(you) is changed into **he** and **1st person **(me) is changed into **him** i.e.according to the **object** (farmer) and the **subject** (foreigner) of the **reporting verb** respectively.

 
 
 

**The final sentence-** *The foreigner asked the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A conjunction is **not** used in the sentence of **wh-family** words **(what, where, who, whom, why, etc.)**.

 
 
• **E.g. **He said to her, "What are you doing these days?"
 
 

 He asked her **what **she was doing those days.

 
• **Change of modals:**

 
 
• Can- could
 
• Will- would
 
• May- might
